summary: US airstrikes destroyed three bridges in Iran's Hormozgan province, killing two and injuring four, while Iranian forces attacked commercial shipping in the Strait of Hormuz and reportedly targeted al-Tanf Garrison in Syria. The Iranian rial hit a record low of 1.918 million rials per dollar as the Health Ministry confirmed 38 dead and over 400 injured since renewed US-Iran fighting. Islamic Resistance in Iraq offered a $10 million bounty for President Trump's assassination as regional proxy threats escalate.

sections.threat_assessment: The conflict has entered a dangerous phase of direct kinetic exchange between US and Iranian forces, with US airstrikes hitting strategic infrastructure inside Iran (bridges in Hormozgan, possible strikes on Bushehr and Shiraz) and Iran retaliating against commercial shipping in the Strait of Hormuz and launching drone strikes against US-linked targets in Kuwait. Iranian proxy threats have escalated to explicit bounties on the US President, while Iranian media claims of attacks on al-Tanf Garrison suggest willingness to target US forces in Syria. The collapse of the Iranian rial and domestic water/electricity shortages indicate severe internal pressure on the Iranian regime, potentially lowering thresholds for further escalation. Israeli operations continue in Gaza and Lebanon but remain secondary to the US-Iran confrontation.
sections.regional_response: Gulf states are experiencing direct spillover: Kuwait hosts wounded personnel and suffered a major drone strike on a US energy contractor facility; UAE reported explosions in Dubai; Bahrain intercepted Iranian airstrikes; Oman saw zero maritime transits in the Strait. Pakistan-Kuwait defense talks reflect Arab Gulf anxiety seeking external security guarantees. Marine traffic has plummeted to eight vessels, all using Iranian waters, indicating a de facto Iranian control of the Strait. Russia diplomatically challenged US justification for strikes. The region is bracing for a heavier second wave of US strikes potentially targeting Tehran, per Axios reporting.
sections.intelligence_notes: Key intelligence gaps include verification of Iranian claims regarding al-Tanf casualties, exact extent of damage to Bushehr nuclear-adjacent facilities, and the status of the MOU referenced by the White House. The UKMTO illegal boarding warning and Yemen ship seizure suggest expanding maritime threat vectors. Iranian domestic infrastructure failures (water, power) may indicate cyber or kinetic targeting beyond acknowledged strikes. The $10 million bounty on Trump by an Iraqi militia signals a significant escalation in proxy-directed assassination threats. Monitoring of Iranian air defense readiness in Shiraz and Bushehr is critical for assessing IRGC capacity to contest further US strikes.
